newsitem.title: VATICAN: Forgiveness is only path to peace, Pope says.
newsitem.headline: Forgiveness is only path to peace, Pope says.

text.p: Pope John Paul said on Wednesday that forgiveness was the only path to peace and urged the world to make 1997 a year of love and reconciliation.

The 76-year-old Pontiff, who lived through World War Two in his native Poland, made his appeal in an Angelus address from the window of his Vatican apartment after celebrating mass at St Peter's Basilica.
The service was held to mark the Roman Catholic feast of the Mother of God and the Church's annual World Peace Day.
"I know how difficult it is to forgive," the Pope said.
"Sometimes it seems really impossible but it is the only way because every vendetta and every act of violence conjures up other vendettas and other acts of violence," he said.
"May the Holy Virgin, the Mother of God, encourage us to begin this new year with a gesture of love and, if necessary, reconciliation, to help build a better world marked by justice and peace".

In a message released in advance last month for the 1997 World Peace Day, the Pope urged a spirit of forgiveness to heal the wounds of ethnic, religious, cultural and spiritual conflict and end what he called a "deadly cycle of revenge".
He spoke favourably in the message of amnesties for crimes committed during armed conflicts, saying such measures helped to cement reconciliation among different groups.
Wednesday's two-hour mass was attended by ambassadors to the Vatican who heard the Pope plead for peace in his homily.

"As we draw to the end of this century in which the world, and especially Europe, have experienced several wars and sufferings, how we would like all men to cross the threshold of the year 2000 in the sign of peace," the Pontiff said.
